turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, mind the step. What can I do for you today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, um, thanks. Err, that car park nearly did me in, we went round and round and Sharon almost collected a ute. Anyway, my back's been crook.
[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): We found a spot in the end. She's been shifting about in the car the whole way.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Forget the car park for a minute. Tell me about the back.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): It's low back pain, and it shoots down my left leg. Three weeks. I was shifting big pot plants and it started that arvo.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Three weeks, down the left leg. How sore is it, and what sets it off?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Sitting's the worst, the desk and the driving. Most days it's a 6 out of 10. Lying down eases it. My colleague Dave reckons these cat stretches off the internet, I had a go and the leg just zinged.
[SEG0008] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She sleeps badly, up and down all night. And she does not take the tablets on Sundays.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah the sleep's right, I can't get comfy. Not Sundays though. I skip Saturdays, after the market I just forget. Sundays I take them.
[SEG0010] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Oh. Saturdays, yeah, market day, my mistake.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the missed day is Saturday. Which tablets, and how much?

[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Ibuprofin, the nurofen, 400 mg by mouth, morning and night. Been the whole three weeks. Takes the edge off. My sister keeps pushing her biotin gummies for her hair, I've never touched them.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Biotin's your sister's, we'll leave that. Any medicine allergies?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none. My husband Barry's on metforman for his diabetes, he's sweet on it, but that's not mine. Oh, the bakery near here does a lamington that's dangerous.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): His metforman, not yours. Any numbness, or weakness, in the leg?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No numbness. The leg's strong, I can still walk the dog. It's just the pain.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any change with the bladder or the bowels, or numbness in the saddle area?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. All normal, thank goodness.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever? Weight coming off?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever, weight's the same. Apart from that lamington, ha.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any cuts or sores that have been slow to heal?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0023] person_3 (CAREGIVER): She nicked her shin on the wheelbarrow. Healed in five days, looked ordinary.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah that one closed right up. Did you see the Swans on the weekend? Hopeless.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Any old back trouble, or operations?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): First time with the back. Appendix out when I was 20, that's it. Desk job at the council, sitting all day, which is not helping.

[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking nerve root pain, the way it shoots and sitting sets it off. First plan in my head is an MRI of the lumbar spine, and maybe a short course of prednisolone to settle the nerve. Let me examine you before I commit.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): An MRI, the tube thing? I get a bit funny in small spaces. Uh, Sharon, did I leave the lights on in the car?
[SEG0029] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Lights are off. She mentioned at the chemist last week her blood pressure was 138 over 86.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Yep, that was last week's chemist one, not today. I told her in the car.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll go with today. Blood pressure is 132 over 84, pulse 76. Hop on the couch and I'll do a straight leg raise.

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Left straight leg raise brings the leg pain on at about 40 degrees. Right side is comfortable to about 70, no pain. Tender over the low lumbar spine. No foot drop, and power's good.

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, thinking it through. That straight leg raise fits a left sided nerve irritation, sciatica, my working impression, not a locked-in diagnosis. No weakness, bladder's fine, only three weeks, and the ibuprofen helps. So I'm changing my mind, no scan yet and no prednisolone.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh good. I wasn't keen on the tube. What do we do instead?

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll refer you to physio, that's the plan. Keep the ibuprofen 400 mg morning and night with food, and try not to skip Saturdays. If you get weakness, bladder trouble, or it's not settling, then we organise an MRI. I'll see you back in six weeks.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Physio, yep. I'll ditch Dave's stretches, they made the leg worse. Six weeks is fine. Short walks with the dog still ok?

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Walking's good, keep them short. Long sitting loads the lower discs and that's why the leg pain fires, so break it up. If you can't pass urine or the leg gives way, don't wait, go to emergency. Reception will book the physio and the six week review.
[SEG0038] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I'll get her to physio. And I'll nag her on Saturdays about the tablets, market or not.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): No worries. Off you go, and mind the step.

spec.situation: Person with low back pain shooting down one leg for three weeks, worse sitting; takes ibuprofen; a colleague's advice on exercises; doctor examines straight-leg raise and plans physio, no scan yet.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.

bad.reason: Transcript mentions husband's diabetes, not family history.

omissions.text: Radiating left leg pain is aggravated by sitting, especially desk work and driving, and relieved by lying down.
Sleep disturbance detail: patient cannot get comfortable and is up and down all night because of the back pain.

No previous back trouble or operations was recorded, but the patient actually denied prior back trouble only; prior surgery history is positive for appendicectomy at age 20, so 'operations absent' would be wrong.
Exam detail missing: left straight leg raise reproduced leg pain at about 40 degrees.
Exam detail missing: right straight leg raise was comfortable to about 70 degrees with no pain.
Doctor explicitly changed plan: no MRI yet and no prednisolone after examination.
Initial but then rejected plan was a short course of prednisolone to settle the nerve.
Doctor advised the patient to take ibuprofen with food.
Safety-net advice missing: seek urgent care/go to emergency if weakness develops, bladder trouble occurs, cannot pass urine, or the leg gives way.
Follow-up logistics: reception will book the physiotherapy and the six-week review.
